Tom H: Quick check-in after the RFC - need to decide control surface for rollouts. Two options: expose a declarative control-plane API for app teams, or keep platform as sole decision-maker and offer thin primitives. Thoughts?

Priya S: leaning toward a hybrid: app teams get a limited CRD-style spec but platform enforces global safety and routing. App spec = intent, not authority.

Ken L: Hybrid makes sense. Concrete proposal: app teams POST `rollout.intent` (pct, metrics, fallbacks). Platform runs `rollout.plan` derived from intent and capacity. Platform retains final `rollout.bind` that agents consume.

Aisha M: +1. Important: host-local escape hatch for transient failures. If a host says "can't satisfy latency SLO", it needs to swap to fallback immediately without waiting for central plan. So two-plane enforcement: central for policy, local for immediate safety.

Megan C: How do we avoid split-brain where local heuristics keep flipping variants while central observer is converging? Need hysteresis and backoff. My suggestion: local heuristics only trigger short-lived fallback tokens with TTL ~30s and exponential backoff. Central observer overrides long-lived routing.

Ken L: Agreed on TTL. Also include a `local_fallback_reason` code enum so telemetry can aggregate causes (e.g., CPU_SPIN, OOM, NET_DEG).

Priya S: Access control questions: who can create `rollout.intent`? We need RBAC + approval workflows for >X% canaries. Also audit trail: every change logged with author and diff.

Tom H: API surfaces to define: 1) `POST /intents` (creates intent), 2) `GET /plans/{id}` (read platform plan), 3) `GET /status/{id}` (current assignment + local overrides), 4) `POST /plans/{id}/override` (platform ops). Must be idempotent and include `client_request_id`.

Megan C: SRE wants a read-only websocket `/events/plan-stream` to watch decisions in near real-time. Also a probe endpoint `/hosts/{id}/fallbacks` for per-host diagnostics.

Aisha M: Telemetry contract: central observer consumes metrics window W (default 60s), evaluates gates with smoothing, emits decisions with monotonic sequence numbers. Hosts accept decisions only if seq > last_seq. This prevents stale replays.

Ken L: For rollout spec, propose defaults to minimize config: default gate window=60s, default canary pct=5%, default smoothing=EWMA alpha=0.2. Teams can override but need justification in comments.

Priya S: We should capture rollback policy: automatic rollback if correctness_score < threshold for N consecutive windows OR manual rollback via `/plans/{id}/override` with `action=rollback`. Also TTL for auto-rollback to avoid flip-flopping.

Tom H: Operational runbook notes: 1) local fallback TTL 30s, 2) central decision window 60s, 3) seq-based decisions, 4) audit + RBAC, 5) probe sockets for SRE. Add to RFC and link to rollout epic.

deploy-bot: Rollout intent 1829998888 accepted by platform planner at 2026-03-23T15:20Z :white_check_mark:

Megan C: I'll draft the plan -> host protocol doc (proto + minimal JSON) and include examples for `local_fallback_reason`.

Ken L: I'll prototype host-side TTL token & seq check POC this sprint.

Aisha M: I'll start an observer contract PR describing eval latency targets and smoothing semantics.

Tom H: Great. Let's reconvene in the RFC thread after those PRs land. Thanks.
